report.summary: Plane definitions and Forest description are unfalsifiable or ambiguous; god-key claim is unfalsifiable as stated.
risks: 5.1 | high | Claim 'Code plane contains files, symbols, functions, methods, syntax and control structure' is ambiguous: 'contains' could mean any or all of these; no operational definition to test. | Propose a concrete list of entities that must be present in a sample Forest instance and check if they are present.

5.2 | high | Claim 'Code plane does not become a fifth "AST plane"' is unfalsifiable because 'becomes' is not defined. | Define observable criteria for when a plane would be considered a new plane (e.g., addition of a new entity type not in the original list).
5.3 | high | Claim 'Type plane contains declared/inferred types, constraints, contracts, interfaces' ambiguous: 'contains' undefined. | Same as 5.1.

5.4 | high | Claim 'Type plane does not become a universal correctness oracle' is unfalsifiable: 'becomes' and 'universal correctness oracle' undefined. | Define what would count as becoming such an oracle (e.g., claiming to prove all program properties).
5.5 | high | Claim 'Data plane contains schemas, tables, fields, formats, fixtures, lineage' ambiguous. | Same as 5.1.

5.6 | high | Claim 'Data plane does not become an unbounded data lake' unfalsifiable: 'becomes' and 'unbounded data lake' undefined. | Define criteria for unbounded data lake (e.g., no schema enforcement).
5.7 | high | Claim 'Knowledge plane contains documentation, ADRs, issues, concepts, claims, wiki links' ambiguous. | Same as 5.1.

5.8 | high | Claim 'Knowledge plane does not become an authority above source/evidence' unfalsifiable: 'authority above' undefined. | Define what would constitute such authority (e.g., accepting knowledge plane statements without source verification).

5.9 | medium | Claim 'Observation, provenance, evidence, and time are orthogonal lineage dimensions, not additional semantic planes' is unfalsifiable: 'orthogonal lineage dimensions' not operationally defined. | Propose a formal definition of orthogonality (e.g., independence of changes) and test with an example.

5.10 | high | Claim 'Forest is the immutable, compiled intermediate representation of one project revision' is ambiguous: 'compiled intermediate representation' not defined. | Specify what the Forest contains (e.g., a set of typed graphs) and verify for a sample revision.

5.11 | medium | Claim 'Forest is not a scheduler, chat memory, archive, or oracle' is a negative claim; unfalsifiable as stated. | Define what would make the Forest a scheduler etc. (e.g., if it schedules tasks), then test.

5.12 | high | Claim 'Sources and candidate trees live in content-addressed storage; the Forest references them and exposes typed intra-plane and verified cross-plane edges' is ambiguous: 'typed intra-plane edges' and 'verified cross-plane edges' not defined. | Specify edge types and verification criteria; test on a sample.

5.13 | high | Claim 'This hypothesis is a god-key candidate, not dogma' is unfalsifiable: 'god-key candidate' undefined. | Define what would falsify it being a god-key (e.g., existence of a better hypothesis).

5.14 | medium | Claim 'It earns its centrality only through the kill criteria in section 13' is unfalsifiable as stated because section 13 is not provided. | Review section 13 and check if kill criteria are falsifiable.
todos: Define each plane's contents operationally (e.g., list of entity types).
Replace 'does not become' claims with explicit criteria that would indicate violation.
Define 'compiled intermediate representation' and 'Forest' contents concretely.
Define 'god-key candidate' or remove the term.
Provide section 13 kill criteria for review.

claims.claim: Code plane contains files, symbols, functions, methods, syntax and control structure.
claims.why: The claim uses 'contains' without specifying what it means for a plane to contain these items. To be falsifiable, one must define observable criteria (e.g., the Forest must have nodes representing each file, symbol, etc.). Without such criteria, no experiment can disprove the claim.

claims.claim: Code plane does not become a fifth 'AST plane'.
claims.why: The term 'becomes' is undefined. To falsify, we need a definition of what would constitute becoming a fifth AST plane (e.g., if the Code plane starts storing AST nodes as separate entities). Without that, the claim cannot be tested.

claims.claim: Type plane contains declared/inferred types, constraints, contracts, interfaces.
claims.why: Same issue as 5.1: 'contains' is not operationally defined.

claims.claim: Type plane does not become a universal correctness oracle.
claims.why: 'Becomes' and 'universal correctness oracle' are undefined. To falsify, specify what would count as becoming such an oracle (e.g., claiming to prove any program property).

claims.claim: Data plane contains schemas, tables, fields, formats, fixtures, lineage.
Data plane does not become an unbounded data lake.
claims.why: 'Becomes' and 'unbounded data lake' undefined. To falsify, define criteria (e.g., no schema enforcement, unlimited storage).

claims.claim: Knowledge plane contains documentation, ADRs, issues, concepts, claims, wiki links.
Knowledge plane does not become an authority above source/evidence.
claims.why: 'Becomes' and 'authority above source/evidence' undefined. To falsify, define what would constitute such authority (e.g., accepting knowledge plane statements without source verification).

claims.claim: Observation, provenance, evidence, and time are orthogonal lineage dimensions, not additional semantic planes.
claims.why: 'Orthogonal lineage dimensions' is not defined operationally. To falsify, one would need a formal definition of orthogonality (e.g., independence of changes) and then test if changes in one dimension affect others.

claims.claim: Forest is the immutable, compiled intermediate representation of one project revision.
claims.why: 'Compiled intermediate representation' is not defined. To falsify, specify what the Forest contains (e.g., a set of typed graphs) and check if a sample Forest meets that definition.

claims.claim: Forest is not a scheduler, chat memory, archive, or oracle.
claims.why: Negative claim with undefined terms. To falsify, define what would make the Forest a scheduler (e.g., if it schedules tasks), then test.

claims.claim: Sources and candidate trees live in content-addressed storage; the Forest references them and exposes typed intra-plane and verified cross-plane edges.
claims.why: Terms 'typed intra-plane edges' and 'verified cross-plane edges' are not defined. To falsify, specify edge types and verification criteria, then test on a sample Forest.

claims.claim: This hypothesis is a 'god-key' candidate, not dogma.
claims.why: 'God-key candidate' is undefined. To falsify, define what would make it a god-key (e.g., a single hypothesis that explains all observations) and what would falsify that status.

claims.claim: It earns its centrality only through the kill criteria in section 13.
claims.why: Section 13 is not provided, so we cannot evaluate whether the kill criteria are falsifiable. The claim itself is contingent on an external reference that is not available.
